narrationScript: Welcome to Chapter 1.5: Quantitative Design Principles in Computer Architecture. This section is all about understanding that good architectural decisions are rooted in data, not just intuition. We'll explore several fundamental principles that guide architects in designing efficient and effective computing systems. By the end of this chapter, you'll be able to apply Amdahl's Law to evaluate the potential speedup of an optimization, a critical skill for performance analysis. You'll also learn how the principle of locality justifies the design of complex cache hierarchies, which are vital for bridging the speed gap between processors and memory. We'll delve into the 'common case fast' principle, understanding why optimizing the most frequent operations is often the most impactful strategy. Finally, we'll analyze the crucial trade-off between performance and cost, using various metrics to make informed design choices. Let's dive into how these principles shape the world of computer architecture.
